quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending. Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: When adjusting your seat for good driving posture, how far should you sit from the steering wheel?

options.text: Six to eight inches.
10 to 12 inches.
18 to 24 inches.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 12 inches.
questions.explanation: Sit 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel. This distance helps protect your head and neck if the airbag deploys during a crash.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always maintain your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line on a highway mean?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You should allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly and are hard to see at night. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly.

questions.question: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?

options.text: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions.
11 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions.
7 o'clock and 5 o'clock positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions.
questions.explanation: Put your left hand at 9 o'clock and your right hand at 3 o'clock on the steering wheel.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The roadway ends ahead.
Drivers must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that the road splits. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to high beam.
Turn your lights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work well with low beams.

questions.question: What does a red-painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: Do not park, stop, or stand at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: If you don't see a gap in freeway traffic when entering, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to find a safe space. Do not stop at the end of the ramp because you won't have room to speed up and match traffic flow.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is blocking your way.
It may help prevent a collision.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to avoid crashes. Do not use it because someone is driving slowly or to tell them to move.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield the right-of-way to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived before you.
Is across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: When changing lanes, check your blind spot by:

options.text: Using your rearview mirror.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
Using your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot see all blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly someone absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Weight, biological sex, and food in the stomach affect alcohol absorption. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: Do not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough for you to safely enter traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mark on streets and highways?

options.text: No passing zones.
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed yellow lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance from other vehicles when it is dark. Use your headlights properly. Do not look at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: What does this sign warn about?

options.text: A right turn.
An intersection.
A lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and prepare to yield or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large truck?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind resistance.
Do not drive next to it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on both sides. Avoid driving beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beams in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
Other drivers will not see you.
Vehicles behind you may get too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beams. The light reflects back at you and makes it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: How do you know what traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: Which action blocks the flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic to back up. Avoid this and keep moving.

questions.question: How do you prevent hydroplaning when it rains?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes your tires to lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous than day driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night you cannot see as far ahead. Oncoming headlights also create glare. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.
